reviews.title: Great App with a Glaring OLED Omission
reviews.text:
This is my preferred calendar but I’ve reached out to the dev asking to add an option for the widgets to have a black OLED option that’s not permanent and adjusts with the system but it doesn’t seem a priority. OLED iPhone’s have been out since 2017, I think it’s time. Currently you can only use dark for widgets with automatic switching between light and dark. You can manually set it up black the widget but only without automatic switching between light. It doesn’t make sense to have a black widget on your Home Screen when the rest of the icons/widgets are light. I’ll adjust to 5 star once added but I really don’t see a reason this isn’t already an option. Especially with the paid version.

Outside of that, great app, great user interface. I also love Cardhop which is included with paid subscription to Flexibits. It still amazes me that such a great Apple developer is missing this feature.

reviews.title: Happily switched to BusyCal
reviews.text:
After about 6 years of using this app with generally positive feelings, the development team decided to add a ‘natural language parser’ that puts what it deems a location/day/time in its proper field. While this seems like a good idea on paper, in practice, it turns out there’s a lot of opportunity for misinterpretation. “Sun” doesn’t always mean Sunday; would you believe sometimes event names reference the actual Sun? The irony that the app thinks the day name should take precedence over what the day was named after in the first place is hilarious. Another: sports games are commonly abbreviated by saying “Away team at Home Team” like Mets at Yankees but the parser interprets this so that the event title will only show the away team and the home team will be buried as the location.

In 2022 I (and many others I’m sure) requested they add an option to disable it and their response to me was that I could put things in quotes so the parser wouldn’t interpret the text. That does work, but I don’t want to do that. I’m not am coder, I’m an end user. In other words, the parser isn’t smart enough, so the user needs to anticipate this by typing more characters.

Guys, your precious parser is not that cool. Give the option to disable it. I’m at the end of my rope—Sorry! I mean “I’m at the end of my rope”.

I’m done waiting. What a stubborn way to lose customers.

reviews.title: $56 a year to use a watch complication! 😂
reviews.text: After using Fantastical for several years, I was disappointed to discover that Apple Watch functionality is now tied to a $56/year Premium subscription/paywall. Worse, the Watch pairing process doesn’t work: the Watch tells me to open Fantastical on my iPhone, but tapping ‘Continue’ does nothing. I updated the app, reinstalled the Watch component, and restarted the devices, with the same result. I understand that developers need to charge for their products, but $56/year for a calendar app—especially when the advertised Watch functionality doesn’t even work—is not something I’m willing to pay for. I’m deleting the app and looking elsewhere.”

reviews.title: Charging for “premium” features?
reviews.text: This is a paid app. I have purchased it separately on my iPhone, iPad, and Android. Over time, this company has started paywalling certain features. Today, I was unable to add an invitee to a meeting. Apparently, this is a premium feature (never had this issue in the past). How can you justify charging for a calendar app and then paywalling a simple feature like editing meeting invites? This is a joke, and I no longer support your app or your company.

reviews.title: It’s gotten so buggy
reviews.text:
I’ve used Fantastical since it was first released years and years ago. The past few years, it seems to forget I added events and show the draft of them when I open the app later, even though the event is already saved to my calendar. The back button on the Location selector screen doesn’t work half the time. It’ll randomly put extra alerts into events that I didn’t choose.

All this is a bummer, because Apple’s calendar app is also terrible. But Fantastical used to be good. I don’t know if they lost the QA team or what, but it’s declined significantly in recent years.

reviews.title: Not Hassle Free
reviews.text:
I wanted to like this app. but It really doesn’t give you much more in useful, everyday features over the iCalendar.  
But my main issue is that it goes out of sync with my iCal on my other devices. 
In order to use the app you have to add your calendar iCloud account and to that, you have to generate a specific password. 
This is the only app that I have that requires this  time consuming hassle. 
Every time it goes out of and I try to re add the app using the app specific password that I previously generated , it isn’t recognized and I have to make another one. 
I’m paying for an app and I have to go through this??? 
I finally gave up and haven’t used this app 8 months. 
It isn’t worth the money for what you get and you go through when it goes out of sync.

reviews.title: It’s unusable now
reviews.text: I’ve been using this app for ten years. I loved so many things about it-especially alerts for travel time. At some point there was an update where almost all events are automatically put in as proposed. So they aren’t really confirmed until you hit confirm. It’s super irritating and some our meetings have just disappeared off the calendar. My assistant has gone back to iCal and now I’m searching for a new calendar app. When are developers going to realize that you don’t need to mess with the simplest and most straightforward things? We just want to input an event. It’s not that deep. There should be a setting to turn this off.
